output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses is most likely caused by the 12 August hardware move of the alarm relay server, not by agency or new nurses. The move was reported as a like-for-like refresh. In fact 11 of the 14 forwarding rules were silently dropped. These included a 15-second hold-off for brief oxygen dips, suppression of repeat notifications, and routing of probe-off and leads-off alarms to the charge phone only. Phone notifications per nurse in Pods A–C doubled from that date, and acknowledgement time roughly doubled. Pod D was still on the old server and saw no change. Bedside alarm volume was flat, which rules out acuity and the monitor software update. Core, agency and new-graduate nurses show similar rates in the affected pods, so staffing mix is not the driver. I am quite confident, about 90%. Do not approve the agency cap or the performance reviews, because they would punish the wrong people. Do not switch off phone forwarding either. Instead, restore the full rule set with Clinical Engineering validation, then track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. The link to rising sick leave is plausible but unproven, since a virus season is also under way. Wireless coverage at room 14 can be checked separately.
